title: Silence, course of dealing, and unsolicited goods
shortTitle: Silence, course of dealing, and unsolicited goods
summary: Silence alone normally does not accept an offer, but established dealings and conduct can give silence significance.
notes: An offeror cannot ordinarily impose acceptance by declaring that failure to reject counts as assent. Hobbs concerns retention of skins after repeated comparable transactions, and American Bronze concerns a longstanding ordering-and-production practice. The book distinguishes these contexts from unsolicited merchandise and from subscriptions in which the recipient has already agreed to a negative-option arrangement. This is a source account, not a current compliance guide.
